courses.title: Python
courses.careerApplications: Used in every subsequent track; the base language for SWE and AI/ML internship applications.

courses.title: Data Structures & Algorithms
courses.careerApplications: The core of coding interview rounds (OAs and live coding).

courses.title: C++ Programming & DSA
courses.careerApplications: Builds the C++ fluency, memory model, STL usage, and DSA implementation skills useful for systems/software engineering and coding interviews.

courses.title: Problem Solving
courses.careerApplications: The actual skill coding interviews are trying to measure.

courses.title: Object-Oriented Programming
courses.careerApplications: Interview topic on its own and the design basis of most production codebases.

courses.title: Git & GitHub
courses.careerApplications: Expected baseline on any engineering team from day one.

courses.title: Linux & Command Line
courses.careerApplications: Assumed knowledge for most backend/infra tasks and technical interviews.

courses.title: SQL
courses.careerApplications: Directly asked about in most SWE and data interviews; used daily on the job.

courses.title: Databases
courses.careerApplications: Schema design and indexing come up in almost every backend interview and every real production incident.

courses.title: APIs
courses.careerApplications: What most backend internship tickets actually involve building.

courses.title: Backend Development
courses.careerApplications: Core skill for backend/SWE internship roles — APIs are what most internship tasks touch.

courses.title: Debugging
courses.careerApplications: Evaluated implicitly in every technical interview and every day on the job.

courses.title: Testing
courses.careerApplications: Increasingly asked about directly; expected of any hire past junior.

courses.title: System Design
courses.careerApplications: Common in later-round SWE interviews, even for some internships.

courses.title: Deep Learning
courses.careerApplications: Needed before LLM/CV/NLP specialization.

courses.title: Transformers
courses.careerApplications: This is the single most valuable architecture to understand deeply for any AI/ML role today — it underlies virtually every state-of-the-art model in language, vision, and beyond.

courses.title: Generative AI
courses.careerApplications: Generative AI is the fastest-growing area of AI hiring; understanding the landscape across model families (not just LLMs) is what separates a generalist AI engineer from a prompt-only user.

courses.title: Large Language Models
courses.careerApplications: Directly relevant if targeting AI-focused roles (e.g. ByteDance AI teams).

courses.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation
courses.careerApplications: A concrete, in-demand AI engineering skill beyond just prompting.

courses.title: AI Agents / Agentic AI
courses.careerApplications: An emerging, differentiating skill for AI/ML engineer roles.

courses.title: Docker
courses.careerApplications: 'It works on my machine' is a real, common failure mode Docker exists to eliminate — expected baseline knowledge for most SWE roles.

courses.title: Hugging Face
courses.careerApplications: The Hugging Face ecosystem is the practical toolkit real AI engineering teams use daily to work with pretrained models -- assumed fluency for most AI/ML roles.

courses.title: Full-Stack Web Integration
courses.careerApplications: Needed for any full-stack or frontend-adjacent SWE role.

courses.title: Model & App Deployment
courses.careerApplications: Turns a working model/app into something a company can actually ship.

courses.title: Kubernetes
courses.careerApplications: ByteDance and most companies running containers at scale expect Kubernetes fluency alongside Docker.

courses.title: Cloud Computing
courses.careerApplications: Nearly every backend/SWE role assumes basic comfort deploying to a cloud provider.

courses.title: Frontend Development
courses.careerApplications: Frontend roles and full-stack roles both expect this; even backend-focused engineers are expected to ship a usable UI.

courses.title: Cybersecurity Fundamentals
courses.careerApplications: Security awareness is now expected baseline knowledge for any backend/SWE role, not a specialist-only concern, and is directly tested in many technical interviews.

courses.title: AI / Machine Learning
courses.careerApplications: Foundation for the AI/ML specialization phase of your roadmap.

courses.title: Data Science
courses.careerApplications: Cleaning and understanding data correctly is the unglamorous 80% of real ML/AI work — and the step where most project failures actually start.

courses.title: Computer Vision
courses.careerApplications: Computer vision roles (autonomous systems, medical imaging, quality inspection) and general AI/ML roles both expect these fundamentals.

courses.title: NLP
courses.careerApplications: Every LLM/AI-agent role builds on these fundamentals; understanding classical NLP also explains why transformers were such a leap forward.

courses.title: GANs
courses.careerApplications: GANs remain relevant for real-time and fast-inference generation use cases even as diffusion models dominate quality benchmarks.

courses.title: VAEs
courses.careerApplications: VAEs' structured, smooth latent spaces are still the go-to choice for representation learning and controllable generation tasks GANs and diffusion handle less naturally.

courses.title: Diffusion Models
courses.careerApplications: Diffusion models are the current state of the art behind most production image/video generation products — directly relevant to any generative-AI-focused role today.

courses.title: Prompt Engineering
courses.careerApplications: Prompt engineering is the fastest, cheapest lever for improving an LLM application's reliability, and is expected working knowledge for any AI-adjacent engineering role today.

courses.title: PyTorch
courses.careerApplications: PyTorch is the dominant framework in research and increasingly in production AI engineering roles — hands-on fluency is directly, frequently tested in AI/ML interviews.

courses.title: TensorFlow
courses.careerApplications: TensorFlow (via Keras) remains widely used in production ML systems, especially where mobile/edge deployment (TensorFlow Lite) or mature MLOps tooling matters.

courses.title: Software Engineering in Practice
courses.careerApplications: Directly used in production teams for code review, maintainability, testing, debugging, collaboration, incident follow-up, and shipping changes safely.

courses.title: Classical AI: Search, Reasoning & Planning
courses.careerApplications: Role-specific company use: search, planning, constraint solving, optimization, robotics, games, scheduling, and rule-based decision systems. Keep it as a specialization, not mandatory daily material for every SWE role.

courses.title: Reinforcement Learning & Modern LLM Post-Training
courses.careerApplications: Role-specific company use: recommendation/decision systems, robotics, RL research, and modern LLM post-training such as preference optimization and RLHF-style pipelines.

courses.title: Large-Scale AI Training & Inference
courses.careerApplications: Role-specific company use for ML infrastructure and platform teams that train or serve large models across multiple GPUs or machines.

courses.title: Interview Preparation
courses.careerApplications: Directly prepares you for the ByteDance-style process and others.

courses.title: Capstone Portfolio
courses.careerApplications: The portfolio proof that converts skill into an offer.

courses.title: Resume Preparation
courses.careerApplications: The resume and portfolio are the gate every application must pass before any human even considers the candidate — polish here directly determines interview volume.

courses.title: Company Preparation
courses.careerApplications: Company-specific preparation is what turns general interview skill into a successful outcome at a SPECIFIC employer, including for processes like ByteDance's.

courses.title: Embedded Systems & Microcontrollers
courses.careerApplications: Role-specific company use in firmware, IoT, robotics, automotive, devices, and hardware-software integration.

courses.title: Systems Programming
courses.careerApplications: Used in infrastructure, performance-sensitive services, runtimes, tooling, operating-system integrations, networking, and low-level debugging roles.

courses.title: Advanced Computer Organization
courses.careerApplications: Role-specific company use in performance engineering, compilers, embedded systems, systems software, accelerators, and hardware-adjacent engineering.
